Q-PC1.title: System Software Architecture Document (SAD)
Q-PC1.description: The SAD describes the top-level structural design of the PP3500 system software: the M-series pump firmware modules (M1–M7), the SaMD/SiMD boundary, the deterministic infusion-control core vs. the AI/ML predictive-alarm envelope, the connectivity-adapter and cloud-suite dependency contracts, and the architectural decisions that satisfy the device requirements. It is the anchor design output that risk, V&V, and trace-matrix activities flow back to.
Q-PC1.why_important_in_project: This is the FDA reviewer's first stop to validate the IEC 62304 Class C software safety classification, the SaMD-vs-SiMD partition, the AI/ML envelope boundary that the LMR2 PCCP-authorized changes target, and the documented dependency on the connectivity-adapter (MDDS) and cloud-suite (non-medical) modules. The SAD also anchors the cybersecurity threat model required by the FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance.

Q-PC25.title: Use Specification (User Needs)
Q-PC25.description: The Use Specification captures the intended-use envelope: who uses the PP3500 (RNs, anesthesiologists, biomedical engineers), where (acute care, ICU, OR, perioperative), under what use scenarios (PCA bolus + continuous infusion, drug library lookup, alarm response), and the user needs each scenario derives. It feeds the IEC 62366-1 usability engineering file and the Design Input Specification.
Q-PC25.why_important_in_project: PCA pumps are alarm-rich, use-error-sensitive devices — the IEC 60601-1-8 alarm scenarios and the AI/ML predictive-alarm UX in LMR2 must trace cleanly to documented user needs. The Use Spec is also the entry point for the summative HF validation under FDA HF Guidance + IEC 62366-1.

Q-PC2.title: Design Input Specification (SRS)
Q-PC2.description: The Software Requirements Specification translates the Use Spec's user needs into testable software requirements covering the deterministic infusion-control core, the alarm subsystem, the drug-library ingest path, the connectivity-adapter interface, the cloud-suite dependency contract, and the AI/ML predictive-alarm envelope (LMR2). Each requirement is uniquely identified and traceable.
Q-PC2.why_important_in_project: The SRS is the regulated design-input artifact under 21 CFR 820.30(c) and the trace anchor for V&V. For PP3500 the SRS must cleanly partition deterministic-vs-AI requirements (so the AI/ML envelope can be PCCP-modified independently), document the drug-library payload contract, and pin the IEC 60601-1-8 alarm requirements that drive the alarm-rich V&V protocols.

Q-PC9.title: Risk Management Report (ISO 14971)
Q-PC9.description: The Risk Management Report consolidates the hazard analysis, risk evaluations, risk controls, and residual-risk acceptability for the PP3500. Q-PC9.why_important_in_project: PCA pumps have one of the highest IEC 60601 risk profiles among infusion devices due to opioid dosing and patient-controlled bolus. ISO 14971 risk evidence is load-bearing for both 510(k) substantial equivalence and the PCCP's benefit-risk reframing for AI/ML modifications. Connects to ENG1 hardware design freeze, ENG11 sensor calibration, and ENG12 alarm conformance.

Q-CA1.title: Adapter SAD
Q-CA1.description: The Connectivity Adapter SAD describes the structural design of the MDDS-class data-transfer middleware that bridges the PP3500 pump and the cloud-suite back-end. Modules include pass-through routing (A3), session control (A4), TLS termination, and the bridge to the management-services interface (MS5). It documents the data-transfer-only boundary that justifies MDDS classification.
Q-CA1.why_important_in_project: Under 21 CFR 880.6310 the connectivity-adapter is a Class I MDDS — exempt from 510(k) premarket submission, but still under 21 CFR 820.30 design controls. The SAD is the primary place the MDDS scope is justified: no clinical decision-making, no patient parameter alteration, data transfer + display only. FDA reviewers walk this to confirm the device is correctly out of the 510(k) burden.

Q-CS1.title: Cloud SAD
Q-CS1.description: The Cloud-Suite Interface Architecture documents the dependency boundary that the regulated devices (PP3500 pump and the MDDS connectivity-adapter) consume from the cloud-suite. Components in scope: drug-library-manager (D-series), fleet-management, compliance-reports, analytics-dashboard, inventory-tracker, alerts-engine, clinical-interface. The SAD focuses on interface contracts, SBOM, storage architecture, and OTA / device-management hooks — not on the cloud features themselves.
Q-CS1.why_important_in_project: Cloud-suite itself is non-medical and is not directly filed under 510(k), but FDA reviewers need to see that the regulated devices' dependency on it is well-characterized. This SAD documents what the pump/adapter expects from the cloud, the trust boundary, and how a cloud-side change can or cannot impact regulated device behavior.

L1-CS24.why_important_in_project: Roll-up to device PSUR keeps cloud-suite signals visible in the regulated post-market loop without duplicating MDR-class reporting.

Q-CS12.title: Cloud Cybersecurity Plan
Q-CS12.description: Cybersecurity plan for the cloud-suite dependency: SBOM (D-series and shared), TLS termination, encryption at rest, multi-tenant isolation, OTA signing service (D4 / ENG7), audit-log integrity (Part 11), vulnerability monitoring, incident response. Maps the cloud side of the regulated-device threat model.
Q-CS12.why_important_in_project: Cloud-suite is the highest-leverage cyber attack surface for the program — a compromise here can deliver a malicious drug-library or firmware to every fielded pump. SBOM transparency, OTA signing, and audit-log integrity are the load-bearing FDA-visible controls.
